root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Bronstein Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qd6 4. d4 Nf6 5. Nf3 a6

overview: Black plays the Gubinsky-Melts ...Qd6 and then adds ...a6, a quiet waiting move that prepares ...Bf5 or ...g6 and denies Bb5 ideas. White has a space advantage and easy development with Nf3, Be3 and Bd3, while Black's position is compact. The play is slow and positional rather than forcing. I know little about the line beyond its reputation as a solid sideline.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Nf3, Be3 and Bd3 and take the space with d4
Look at Nb5 ideas if the queen leaves the d6 square
Castle and attack with e4-e5 or Nd5

black_ideas.idea: Keep the queen on d6, castle and challenge with ...c5
Trade pieces to ease the cramp

typical_structures.structure: White d4 against Black pawns on a6, e6/g6
Black queen on d6 on the semi-open d-file

character.notes: Black holds a solid cramped position and White has some lead in space but no attack.

gambit.notes: The d5 pawn is recaptured immediately.

soundness.notes: Sound, a sideline of a respectable line.

structure.notes: Scandinavian semi-open with the queen on d6.

approach.notes: Less common than the main Scandinavian lines but played by strong players now and then, so standard with low confidence.

level.notes: Plans are clear and there is little to memorise.

character.reason: Compact Black set-up with few weaknesses.

approach.reason: Less common, but a normal sideline.

plans.reason: White has the space; Black must hold.
